options.C: Natural suction created by the drainage bag
options.D: A water-filled balloon at the tip

explanation: Correct! Once the catheter is inside the bladder, sterile water fills a tiny balloon at the end, acting like an anchor so it doesn't slip out.

question: In patients with high blood pressure, what common recovery factor can trigger a dangerous blood pressure spike?

options.A: Pain and anxiety
options.B: Sleeping on the left side
options.C: Eating fresh vegetables
options.D: Drinking too much water

explanation: When a patient feels pain or emotional stress, their nervous system kicks in, which can cause their blood pressure to shoot up.

question: What is a common community-level effect when mental health struggles go untreated for too long?

options.A: Higher local crop yields due to increased community labor
options.B: Decreased need for public transportation infrastructure
options.C: Increased strain on emergency services and public health systems
options.D: Immediate elimination of all local economic taxation policies

explanation: Correct! When people don't get support early, emergency rooms, local clinics, and public health resources end up carrying a very heavy load.

question: What is the main psychological feature of illness anxiety disorder (hypochondriasis)?

options.A: Complete lack of awareness regarding bodily changes
options.B: Intentional simulation of physical disease for attention
options.C: Frequent hallucinations involving internal organ failure
options.D: Excessive anxiety about having a serious illness

explanation: You've got this! The core thing to remember here is constant, overwhelming worry about having a severe medical condition, even when medical tests show everything is fine.

question: What is the very first thing you should do if you realize a medication error has happened?

options.A: Write an angry message in the chat group for the next shift
options.B: Call the hospital lawyer to prepare legal defense documents
options.C: Hide the empty medication wrapper in a pocket to destroy evidence
options.D: Assess the patient's clinical condition and provide any needed emergency care

explanation: The patient always comes first! Checking on their physical condition and providing any necessary care takes priority over paperwork and reporting.

question: Who carries the biggest responsibility for building a safe culture in a hospital?

options.A: Patients and their visiting family members
options.B: Hospital leadership and nurse managers
options.C: External pharmaceutical manufacturing companies
options.D: Newly graduated student nurses on ward rotation

explanation: Spot on! Management sets the tone, provides the right tools, and creates policies that make a safe workplace possible.

question: Which detail is most important for a home nurse to record during feeding visits?

options.A: Estimated percentage of meals eaten and weight trends
options.B: The exact brand of dishes used in the household
options.C: The grocery store prices of all purchased food
options.D: The names of visiting neighbors and friends

explanation: You got it! Tracking intake percentages and weight changes tells you clearly if the nutrition plan is working.

question: Why is covering up a clinical error instead of reporting it an ethical violation?

options.A: It puts the patient at ongoing risk and breaks professional trust
options.B: It violates federal tax codes regarding hospital accounting
options.C: It prevents the hospital from collecting insurance money
options.D: It forces senior doctors to take over daily bedside nursing duties

explanation: Exactly. Hiding mistakes leaves patients vulnerable to repeat errors and goes against our core duty of honesty and safety.

question: What distinct, tough patch does the diphtheria bacterium form in the throat?

options.A: A tough gray pseudomembrane
options.B: A widespread fatty liver
options.C: A fluid-filled skin blister
options.D: A hard calcified granuloma

explanation: Diphtheria creates a stubborn gray coating (pseudomembrane) in the airway made of dead cells, bacteria, and clotting proteins that can block breathing.

question: Why do workers sometimes hide minor injuries instead of visiting the clinic?

options.A: Not knowing the clinic is open in the mornings
options.B: Fear of losing pay or facing disciplinary action from management
options.C: Thinking safety nurses only handle major surgeries
options.D: Preferring traditional herbs for all injuries

explanation: Sad but true—many workers worry they will get punished, lose wages, or risk their jobs if they report small accidents.

question: How do large conferences usually differ from smaller seminars in nursing education?

options.A: Seminars always last for an entire week while conferences last only one hour.
options.B: Seminars focus exclusively on international health policies rather than clinical work.
options.C: Conferences are larger gatherings covering broad trends and offering networking opportunities.
options.D: Conferences are strictly hands-on practical sessions held in small hospital rooms.

explanation: Think of a conference as a big gathering where nurses from all over meet to share big ideas and research, while seminars are smaller, cozy deep-dives into specific topics.

question: Why is having 'zero complaints' from nurses NOT always a sign that a hospital software program is working well?

options.A: Nurses may have given up or created workarounds instead of reporting issues
options.B: Hospital computers block all feedback messages sent by staff
options.C: Software automatically fixes its own design errors over time
options.D: Nurses prefer spending extra hours clicking through bad menus

explanation: So true! When systems are frustrating, busy nurses often just find quiet workarounds instead of wasting time filing formal complaints.

question: Why does a failure in cell death (apoptosis) lead to autoimmune disease?

options.A: Bone marrow stops making new white blood cells
options.B: Pathogens are allowed to hide inside dying cells
options.C: Healthy cells die too quickly and release too many nutrients
options.D: Autoreactive lymphocytes survive instead of undergoing programmed cell death

explanation: Normally, rogue immune cells that could attack our body are told to self-destruct. When that fails, these harmful cells stick around and cause trouble.

question: Why are lab tests (biochemical assessments) super helpful in nutrition compared to just looking at a patient?

options.A: It detects deficiencies before physical symptoms appear.
options.B: It requires no special patient preparation.
options.C: It is much cheaper than physical examinations.
options.D: It replaces the need for a dietary history.

explanation: You've got this! Lab tests reveal hidden nutritional shortages long before the body starts showing visible signs. Think of it as an early warning system!

question: Why is proper clinical notes sent along with an emergency referral so important?

options.A: It acts as a formal receipt for community transport payment
options.B: It prevents the receiving hospital from asking any questions
options.C: It provides essential clinical history to speed up hospital treatment
options.D: It gives the referral team legal protection against lawsuits

explanation: You nailed it! Sharing past findings, treatments given, and vitals helps the hospital team jump right into action without wasting precious time repeating tests.

question: What is the primary reason for keeping completed research questionnaires in a locked cabinet?

options.A: To ensure the forms do not get misplaced by staff
options.B: To make sure nobody steals the paper pens
options.C: To protect patient confidentiality and privacy
options.D: To comply with hospital interior design rules

explanation: Securing completed research documents is an ethical duty to protect participants' private health information. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h8)

question: Why does the human body need food nutrients?

options.A: To completely prevent all known infectious diseases
options.B: To speed up the physical digestion of solid wastes
options.C: To increase the total volume of blood in circulation
options.D: To provide substances needed for energy, growth, and repair

explanation: Think of nutrients as the fuel and building blocks your body uses every single day to stay active, grow, and heal wounds. You've got this!

question: Why doesn't having plenty of food in the country automatically mean everyone is well-nourished?

options.A: Government regulations legally restrict citizens from buying more than basic rations
options.B: Local populations automatically reject imported food items due to personal preferences
options.C: Stored food spoils instantly before it can be transported to local neighborhood markets
options.D: Food may be present in the country but remain unaffordable or inaccessible to poor households

explanation: Just because food is in the country doesn't mean poor families have the money to buy it. Distribution and wealth play huge roles!

question: If someone suffers from lead poisoning, what type of epidemiological agent is at fault?

options.A: A biological agent
options.B: A nutritional agent
options.C: A physical agent
options.D: A chemical agent

explanation: Poisons, toxins, and heavy metals are chemical agents because they cause harm through chemical reactions in the body.

question: Why do nursing students need to choose their research topics carefully?

options.A: So the hospital management can pay for their tuition
options.B: Because clinical time and research resources are limited
options.C: To completely eliminate all diseases from the ward
options.D: To ensure the final paper is published in a foreign journal

explanation: Time and materials are precious when you're balancing ward work and studies, so picking a focused topic helps you make every effort count!

question: What is a primary immunodeficiency disorder?

options.A: Something that only affects adults over sixty
options.B: An issue triggered by common painkillers
options.C: An inherited genetic defect present right from birth
options.D: A condition caused by severe physical trauma later in life

explanation: Think of 'primary' as being born with it. These disorders stem from gene mutations passed down from parents, unlike secondary ones that happen later in life.

question: In clinical practice, what do healthcare standards actually give us?

options.A: A formula for calculating hospital budgets
options.B: A list of punishments for clinical errors
options.C: A yardstick for measuring safe and competent performance
options.D: A strict schedule for nurse shift rotations

explanation: Spot on! Standards act as our baseline guide or 'yardstick' to make sure our nursing care is always safe, skilled, and professional.

question: Which tiny, hair-like parts of the respiratory tract get paralyzed and destroyed by cigarette smoke?

options.A: Cilia
options.B: Alveoli
options.C: Bronchioles
options.D: Pleura

explanation: Cilia are the tiny sweeping brushes of the lungs that clear out mucus and dirt. Smoke damages them badly, but understanding this puts you one step ahead!

question: What is the first-line drug treatment for a patient with symptomatic bradycardia?

options.A: Amiodarone
options.B: Sodium bicarbonate
options.C: Adenosine
options.D: Atropine

explanation: Atropine blocks the vagus nerve to help speed up a dangerously slow heart rate. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T4#GNS315_U4_T4_h6)

question: What structural feature inside lymphatic vessels prevents the backward flow of lymph?

options.A: Valves
options.B: Nodes
options.C: Sphincters
options.D: Cilia

explanation: Lymphatic vessels contain one-way valves that ensure fluid moves only toward the heart. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h2)

question: Which of the following is an example of non-verbal communication that can significantly influence a patient interaction?

options.A: The specific medical terminology used in the care plan
options.B: Open posture and relaxed facial expressions
options.C: A printed schedule of clinic operating hours
options.D: The speed at which discharge instructions are read aloud

explanation: Body language, posture, and facial expressions are non-verbal cues that convey openness, empathy, or disinterest without using words. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T23#GNS225_U2_T23_h2)

question: How do researchers usually find common themes in qualitative interview notes?

options.A: By selecting only the longest interview and ignoring all the others
options.B: By throwing away any interview answer that does not match their personal opinion
options.C: By reading through the text repeatedly to identify patterns and grouping similar ideas
options.D: By feeding every sentence into a calculator to find the mathematical mean

explanation: Thematic analysis takes patience: researchers read the text over and over to spot patterns and group similar ideas together.

question: What is the primary focus of social services in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Performing major orthopedic surgeries in the operating theatre
options.B: Addressing non-medical social and economic challenges affecting health
options.C: Conducting laboratory blood tests and urinalysis
options.D: Prescribing strong antibiotics for bacterial infections

explanation: Good health isn't just about medicine! Social services look at things like poverty, living conditions, and family support that affect how well a patient recovers.

question: What is a very common cause of a large bowel obstruction?

options.A: Eating too much high-fiber food at one meal
options.B: A mild viral stomach flu causing diarrhea
options.C: An overgrowth of normal intestinal bacteria
options.D: Colorectal cancer or a twisted bowel loop

explanation: Correct! Tumors growing inside the colon or a loop of bowel twisting on itself (volvulus) are major physical reasons the large intestine gets blocked.

question: How can hospital management best help nurses overcome barriers to using research?

options.A: Requiring every nurse to publish a textbook before promotion
options.B: Providing access to journal databases and encouraging ward journal clubs
options.C: Punishing nurses who ask questions about traditional ward routines
options.D: Banning all clinical discussions during the morning handover shift

explanation: Brilliant! Creating an encouraging learning environment with easy resource access makes research feel friendly and doable for the whole team.

question: During a clinical assessment, what should a nurse focus on documenting when evaluating a patient's personality style?

options.A: Unproven childhood fantasies
options.B: Personal moral judgments and opinions
options.C: Objective behaviors and interactions
options.D: Derogatory character labels

explanation: Nurses must remain professional and record clear, objective observations of patient behavior rather than personal judgments. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T8#GNS314_U1_T8_h5)

question: What does 'out-of-pocket health expenditure' mean for an ordinary patient in Nigeria?

options.A: Receiving free medical care funded by international grants
options.B: Paying cash directly to providers at the point of service
options.C: Deducting healthcare costs from monthly cooperative savings
options.D: Using a comprehensive health insurance prepaid card

explanation: Out-of-pocket spending simply means paying cash right there at the hospital counter when you get sick. It's the daily reality for many Nigerians!

question: When mistakes happen in the clinic, what is usually the real root cause?

options.A: Flawed system designs interacting with human limits
options.B: Poor physical fitness and lack of sleep
options.C: A lack of basic nursing education among staff
options.D: Intentional negligence by individual healthcare workers

explanation: You're doing great! Remember that most clinical errors happen because the work environment and tools don't properly support natural human limits—not because nurses are careless.

question: Why is keeping a detailed maintenance log for cold chain equipment important?

options.A: It allows staff to test the freezing point of water ice
options.B: It reduces the amount of electricity the refrigerator uses
options.C: It helps plan for timely repairs and equipment replacements
options.D: It replaces the need to check temperatures twice daily

explanation: Maintenance logs track the performance history of appliances, making it easier to justify buying replacements before breakdowns occur. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h8)

question: What does the round window do when the stapes pushes inward against the oval window?

options.A: It pulls inward to trap the sound waves inside the cochlea
options.B: It vibrates at a higher frequency to match the malleus
options.C: It bulges outward to relieve fluid pressure in the cochlea
options.D: It seals shut to protect the delicate hair cells from damage

explanation: Since fluid cannot be squished into a smaller space, the round window acts as a pressure-relief valve, bulging outward every time the oval window pushes in.

question: Your patient takes a traditional herbal remedy along with their prescribed blood pressure drugs. What should you do?

options.A: Explore the cultural significance of the remedy and check for potential drug interactions
options.B: Confiscate the herbal preparation during the home visit
options.C: Tell the patient immediately that traditional remedies are completely useless
options.D: Ignore the herbal remedy since it is not part of the hospital chart

explanation: Never dismiss cultural practices! Respect the patient while smartly checking to ensure the herbs won't clash with their prescribed medications.

question: How do upfront hospital user fees usually affect patients with little income?

options.A: They are given free medications upon arrival
options.B: They are automatically transferred to private suites
options.C: They receive faster treatment than wealthy patients
options.D: They delay seeking care until their condition worsens

explanation: Exactly right. Worrying about money often causes vulnerable patients to stay home until a simple illness turns into a major emergency.

question: What makes amiodarone different from most other antiarrhythmic medications?

options.A: It is completely cleared from the human body within two hours of a dose
options.B: It cannot be given intravenously under any emergency circumstances
options.C: It displays properties from all four Vaughan Williams classes of medications
options.D: It only works when taken alongside a high-fat meal to help absorption

explanation: Amiodarone is a broad-spectrum drug that blocks sodium, potassium, and calcium channels while also acting as a beta-blocker. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h5)

question: What does the term 'dual diagnosis' mean in psychiatric care?

options.A: A patient is evaluated by two different doctors on the same day
options.B: A patient has two different physical infections at the same time
options.C: A patient requires two different types of surgical operations
options.D: A patient has both a mental illness and a substance use disorder

explanation: Dual diagnosis describes individuals who experience a co-occurring psychiatric condition and substance use problem simultaneously. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of secondary prevention in healthcare?

options.A: Long-term physical rehabilitation
options.B: Early detection and treatment
options.C: Providing end-of-life comfort care
options.D: Stopping disease before it starts

explanation: Secondary prevention catches health issues early through screening so treatment can stop the disease from getting worse. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T4#GNS225_U2_T4_h1)

question: What makes home health nursing quite different from working in a hospital ward?

options.A: Infection rates are automatically zero in residential homes
options.B: Patients receive no medical equipment at home
options.C: The nurse has less direct control over the physical environment
options.D: Family members are strictly prohibited from providing care

explanation: Unlike neat hospital wards, homes vary a lot in layout and cleanliness! You have to adapt your nursing care to fit the patient's actual living space.

question: What important advice should you give a patient who wants to start taking a daily multivitamin?

options.A: Taking five times the recommended dose will speed up healing
options.B: Natural supplements never interact with prescribed heart medications
options.C: Supplements do not replace the benefits of eating a balanced, whole-food diet
options.D: There is no need to tell the doctor about over-the-counter vitamins

explanation: Real, whole foods give our bodies natural fiber and nutrients that pills just cannot completely copy. Supplements are helpers, not food substitutes!

question: Why is priority setting necessary during community mobilisation?

options.A: Resources are limited, so the community must focus on the most pressing problem
options.B: It stops people from talking during community meetings
options.C: Nurses are not allowed to work on more than two diseases at a time
options.D: The government requires every village to solve exactly one problem per year

explanation: Because time, money, and materials are limited, communities must rank their problems and tackle the most urgent ones first. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h5)

question: While helping a patient walk, you notice their urine bag is hanging higher than their bladder. Why is this a problem?

options.A: Urine can flow backward into the bladder and cause an infection
options.B: The urine output will instantly turn bright red with blood
options.C: The plastic collection tubing will melt from body heat
options.D: The catheter balloon will automatically pop from the extra pressure

explanation: Gravity works both ways! If the bag is higher than the bladder, contaminated urine can flow right back inside and give the patient a nasty urinary tract infection.

question: In public health, what do we mean by 'nutritional deserts' in cities?

options.A: Dry geographic regions where no plants can ever grow
options.B: Neighborhoods that have an excess of community gardens
options.C: Industrial zones dedicated exclusively to meat processing
options.D: Areas with limited access to fresh, affordable, and healthy food

explanation: Correct! Nutritional deserts are urban spots where residents find it really hard to grab fresh, healthy food nearby.

question: What is the main job of secondary lymphoid organs like lymph nodes?

options.A: To destroy immature white blood cells before they enter circulation
options.B: To filter pathogens from lymph and activate adaptive immune cells
options.C: To manufacture red blood cells during severe systemic infection
options.D: To produce brand new stem cells for the circulatory system

explanation: Exactly! Lymph nodes act like security checkpoints, trapping germs so immune cells can meet them and start a fight.

question: What is the primary focus of microbiology in nursing practice?

options.A: Synthesizing new pharmaceutical drugs in the ward
options.B: Calculating precise fluid balance for dehydrated patients
options.C: Understanding microscopic organisms and how they spread
options.D: Operating advanced diagnostic laboratory machinery

explanation: Microbiology studies tiny organisms like bacteria and viruses so nurses can understand how they cause disease and how to stop them. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h1)

question: How do EMR systems help stop medication mistakes compared to old paper charts?

options.A: By eliminating the problem of misreading messy handwriting
options.B: By automatically administering drugs without nurse approval
options.C: By letting patients prescribe their own medication at home
options.D: By completely removing the need for doctors to write orders

explanation: We've all squinted at difficult handwriting! Clear digital text keeps patients safe by taking the guesswork out of doctor's orders.

question: What standard assessment tool do nurses use to monitor patients for early signs of tardive dyskinesia?

options.A: APGAR scoring system
options.B: Braden Scale for Pressure Ulcers
options.C: AIMS (Abnormal Involuntary Movement Scale)
options.D: Glasgow Coma Scale

explanation: We use the AIMS scale during regular check-ups to score any involuntary twitching or movements so we catch tardive dyskinesia early.

question: Which two hormones does the anterior pituitary gland release to directly stimulate the ovaries?

options.A: FSH and LH
options.B: Estrogen and progesterone
options.C: Prolactin and cortisol
options.D: GnRH and oxytocin

explanation: Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH) are the dynamic duo released by the pituitary gland to wake up the ovaries and get things moving.

question: What is the primary benefit of enrolling a patient in a structured cardiac rehabilitation program?

options.A: Providing a surgical alternative to coronary artery bypass grafting
options.B: Improving overall physical conditioning and reducing future heart risks
options.C: Ensuring the patient never has to take prescription medications again
options.D: Eliminating the need for routine follow-up visits with the cardiologist

explanation: Cardiac rehabilitation helps patients regain strength, manage risk factors, lower stress, and significantly reduce the likelihood of future cardiac events. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T13#GNS213_U1_T13_h6)

question: Which lab values must a nurse check before a patient receives gadolinium contrast dye for an MRI?

options.A: Fasting blood glucose and hemoglobin A1c
options.B: Kidney function tests like creatinine and BUN
options.C: Liver enzymes and total protein counts
options.D: Complete blood count and platelet levels

explanation: Contrast dye is filtered through the kidneys, so poor kidney function can lead to dangerous complications like nephrogenic systemic fibrosis. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h5)

question: What is the main job of the National Commission for Persons with Disabilities?

options.A: To manage shipping ports and maritime trade
options.B: To enforce laws protecting the rights and inclusion of persons with disabilities
options.C: To provide military combat training for citizens
options.D: To oversee the building of telecom masts

explanation: Correct! This commission exists to make sure individuals living with disabilities have their rights protected and are fully included in society.

question: What is the absolute first priority when managing a severely injured teenager in the emergency unit?

options.A: Securing the airway and stabilizing breathing
options.B: Calling the legal authorities for documentation
options.C: Asking about the history of the quarrel
options.D: Administering long-term psychiatric counseling

explanation: You got it! In emergency trauma care, the primary survey always comes first—focusing on airway, breathing, and circulation to keep the patient alive.

question: How can severe arthritis make mealtime a struggle for a home care patient?

options.A: By making it painful and difficult to hold utensils and feed oneself
options.B: By preventing the stomach from properly absorbing essential vitamins
options.C: By causing a complete loss of taste perception in the tongue
options.D: By drastically increasing the body's daily metabolic calorie requirements

explanation: Stiff, painful joints make holding a spoon or fork really frustrating. When feeding hurts, patients naturally eat less, so adaptive utensils can be a game-changer!

question: What is the biggest weakness of using the rational (logical) method by itself?

options.A: It cannot be written down on paper or spoken aloud
options.B: It ignores all forms of mathematical calculation
options.C: A flawed starting premise leads to an incorrect conclusion
options.D: It takes too many years to complete a single calculation

explanation: Logic is only as good as its starting point. If your first assumption is wrong, your final answer will be wrong too!

question: Which systemic autoimmune condition is a common underlying cause of chronic glomerulonephritis?

options.A: Systemic lupus erythematosus
options.B: Chronic asthma
options.C: Iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Rheumatoid arthritis only

explanation: Lupus (SLE) is a well-known condition where the body's immune system attacks its own tissues, very frequently targeting the delicate filters in the kidneys.

question: Your patient just had surgery and has painful trapped gas. What is the best first nursing action?

options.A: Insert a rigid nasogastric tube immediately without a doctor's order.
options.B: Assist the patient to ambulate in the hallway or change positions in bed.
options.C: Instruct the patient to hold the gas in to prevent embarrassment.
options.D: Administer strong intravenous narcotics for pain relief.

explanation: Movement is medicine! Getting a post-op patient walking or shifting positions wakes up the bowels and helps release gas naturally.

question: Which of these is a known risk factor for developing severe menstrual cramps?

options.A: Living in a warm tropical climate
options.B: Starting menstrual periods at a very early age
options.C: Having a short duration of menstrual bleeding
options.D: Starting menstruation after age sixteen years

explanation: Correct! Early menarche (getting your period before age 11) is linked to a higher chance of primary dysmenorrhoea.

question: Why are art and creative therapies so helpful for trauma survivors?

options.A: They replace the need for professional psychiatric counseling
options.B: They completely cure post-traumatic stress disorder in one session
options.C: They allow expression of emotions that are hard to put into words
options.D: They force patients to relive painful memories out loud

explanation: Trauma can be really tough to talk about. Creative outlets like drawing or painting give patients a safe way to let those heavy feelings out.

question: What complex surgery involves removing the head of the pancreas, the duodenum, and the gallbladder?

options.A: Whipple procedure
options.B: Cholecystostomy
options.C: Splenectomy
options.D: Gastric bypass

explanation: The Whipple procedure is a major operation performed to treat tumors located in the head of the pancreas. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h7)

question: Which of the following is an example of a descriptive statistic?

options.A: A surgical success prediction model
options.B: The exact biological cause of a virus mutation
options.C: A proven cure rate for a genetic disorder
options.D: Percentage of patients with high blood pressure

explanation: Numbers like percentages, averages, and counts are classic descriptive statistics that simply summarize what is happening in the data. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h6)

question: A family member is sitting quietly at the bedside crying after a loss. What is the most caring nursing action?

options.A: Sit quietly beside the family member and offer a comforting presence
options.B: Leave the room immediately so the family can have complete privacy
options.C: Encourage the person to cheer up by remembering happier times
options.D: Administer a prescribed sedative to help the person calm down

explanation: Well done! Sometimes silence and a warm, supportive presence speak louder than any words can.

question: Why do patients with acute viral hepatitis develop jaundice (yellow eyes and skin)?

options.A: The gallbladder ruptures and releases stored bile directly into the abdominal cavity
options.B: Swelling in the liver blocks bile flow, causing bilirubin to back up into the blood
options.C: Red blood cells multiply too quickly for the bone marrow to keep up with them
options.D: The kidneys stop filtering waste products due to a sudden drop in blood pressure

explanation: When the liver is swollen, normal bile drainage gets blocked. This backs up yellow bilirubin pigments into the bloodstream, turning the skin and eyes yellow.

question: What is the main goal of an endocrine suppression test?

options.A: To measure how fast the kidneys reabsorb glucose from the urine
options.B: To see if a gland stops producing hormones when given a suppressing agent
options.C: To stimulate a sleeping gland into producing maximum hormone levels
options.D: To permanently destroy overactive cells inside the adrenal cortex

explanation: Exactly! While stimulation tests wake glands up, suppression tests check if an overactive gland knows how to quiet down when it's supposed to.

question: Which of these is NOT a good practice when trying to prevent adverse drug reactions?

options.A: Guessing the patient's weight without asking them
options.B: Checking the patient's allergy history before giving drugs
options.C: Asking about local herbs and supplements
options.D: Following the five rights of medication administration

explanation: Never guess! Drug doses must be exact, especially for vulnerable patients. Always measure or ask for accurate weights.

question: Why should nurses be quick to spot the difference between side effects and true adverse drug reactions?

options.A: To know which symptoms require immediate clinical action versus routine monitoring
options.B: To ensure the patient stops paying for their hospital admission
options.C: To calculate the exact lethal dose for the patient chart
options.D: To prevent the hospital pharmacy from purchasing the drug again

explanation: Catching harm early lets you protect your patient fast and report things properly. Brilliant nursing care in action!

question: A patient with active tuberculosis usually reports which set of body-wide signs?

options.A: Sudden weight gain, severe headache, and lethargy
options.B: Night sweats, low-grade fevers, and weight loss
options.C: Constipation, blurred vision, and muscle spasms
options.D: High fever, severe joint swelling, and a skin rash

explanation: Active TB drains the body's energy. Classic signs include drenching night sweats, afternoon fevers, and losing weight without trying.

question: What main heart rhythm is an AED built to fix with an electrical shock?

options.A: Ventricular fibrillation
options.B: Sinus bradycardia
options.C: First-degree heart block
options.D: Atrial flutter

explanation: An AED is designed to step in during life-threatening rhythms like ventricular fibrillation, resetting the heart's electrical system so it can beat normally again.

question: Where are most private hospitals and well-equipped health facilities concentrated in Nigeria?

options.A: Isolated coastal fishing ports
options.B: Nomadic desert settlements
options.C: Urban centers and major cities
options.D: Remote rural farming villages

explanation: Private investors tend to set up where business is booming, meaning big cities get better equipped facilities than rural areas.

question: Why is reuniting families so important right after a disaster strikes?

options.A: It replaces the need for any medical triage assessments.
options.B: It helps restore the survivor's sense of safety and emotional control.
options.C: It guarantees the patient will never develop any physical illnesses.
options.D: It reduces the administrative burden on hospital billing departments.

explanation: Spot on! Finding loved ones helps chip away at the terrible isolation and panic that comes with a traumatic event, helping survivors feel secure again.

question: A community health nurse in a rural Nigerian village organizes an outreach to teach mothers how to mix oral rehydration salts for diarrhea. What type of intervention is this?

options.A: A purely administrative task unrelated to patient welfare
options.B: A tertiary action meant exclusively for chronic surgical patients
options.C: An unnecessary hospital procedure reserved only for intensive care units
options.D: A practical community-level nursing intervention promoting health recovery

explanation: Community outreach brings essential health knowledge directly to where people live to prevent severe illness. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T5#GNS123_U1_T5_h6)

question: A cancer patient on chemotherapy develops a fever and oral thrush. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: The chemotherapy drug caused an allergic reaction on the skin.
options.B: The cancer cells mutated into a bacterial infection.
options.C: The treatment suppressed the immune system, allowing a fungus to overgrow.
options.D: The patient ate too much sugar before coming to the hospital.

explanation: Exactly! Chemo lowers white blood cells, giving everyday germs and fungi like thrush an easy chance to take over.

question: A ward manager wants to change wound care based on one small, poorly designed study. What should the staff nurse do first?

options.A: Critique the study to see if the methods support the new practice
options.B: Report the journal publisher to the nursing council
options.C: Immediately adopt the new method without reading the paper
options.D: Refuse to do any wound care for the patients

explanation: Before changing clinical routines, nurses should examine the strength and validity of the underlying research. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h2)

question: When would a clinician choose indirect ophthalmoscopy over direct ophthalmoscopy?

options.A: When performing a quick bedside neurological check on a ward
options.B: When examining the far periphery of the entire retina
options.C: When only a small portion of the central optic disc needs viewing
options.D: When the patient cannot tolerate any bright light shining near them

explanation: Indirect ophthalmoscopy provides a much wider, stereoscopic view that allows the examiner to see the far edges of the retina. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h3)

question: How should you talk to a patient or their family after an adverse clinical event?

options.A: Using complex clinical terms to explain the error
options.B: By directing all questions exclusively to the hospital lawyer
options.C: Using clear language free of heavy medical jargon
options.D: By writing a formal letter without speaking directly

explanation: Families going through a tough time need simple, plain language they can easily understand, not confusing medical terms.

question: What is the primary goal of person-centered care in modern long-term facilities?

options.A: To honor individual resident preferences, choices, and daily routines
options.B: To reduce operating costs by standardizing all resident meals
options.C: To enforce strict schedules that make facility operations more efficient
options.D: To eliminate the need for any licensed nursing staff on site

explanation: Person-centered care puts the resident first! Instead of forcing everyone onto a rigid hospital schedule, it revolves around what the individual patient actually likes and prefers.

question: What is the specialized name for the plasma membrane of a skeletal muscle fiber?

options.A: Sarcoplasmic reticulum
options.B: Sarcoplasm
options.C: Sarcolemma
options.D: Sarcomere

explanation: The sarcolemma is the cell membrane surrounding a skeletal muscle fiber. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h3)

question: Which sign shows mental fatigue in neurasthenia?

options.A: Sudden loss of consciousness
options.B: Uncontrollable muscle twitching
options.C: Poor memory and reduced concentration
options.D: Auditory and visual hallucinations

explanation: Great try! Mental tiredness directly affects your brain's ability to focus and remember things. You're building solid clinical instincts!

question: Why is proper nutrition considered a core element of Primary Health Care?

options.A: Nutrition is only important for professional athletes
options.B: Good nutrition strengthens immunity and prevents infectious diseases
options.C: Eating expensive foreign food cures chronic illnesses
options.D: Food supply is managed strictly by the federal military

explanation: Well-nourished bodies fight off infections much more effectively, reducing the burden of disease in the community. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the very first step in the MBO cycle within a healthcare organization?

options.A: Conducting the final end-of-year staff performance review
options.B: Purchasing new medical equipment for the wards
options.C: Executive leadership defining broad strategic goals
options.D: Punishing departments that failed previous targets

explanation: The MBO process starts at the top, giving a clear direction that individual departments can then break down. [learn more](GST321_U2_T5#GST321_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of the Incident Command System during a disaster?

options.A: To place financial responsibility solely on local nursing staff
options.B: To establish a clear chain of command and organized coordination
options.C: To allow every responder to make independent medical decisions
options.D: To eliminate the need for medical triage protocols

explanation: Well done! This system keeps everyone organized with clear leadership roles, stopping chaos and confusion when multiple agencies respond.

question: What is a major communication benefit of implementing MBO in a clinical setting?

options.A: It allows doctors to bypass nurses when giving patient orders
options.B: It completely replaces all written patient health records
options.C: It opens up constructive feedback channels between staff and management
options.D: It stops patients from complaining about hospital food

explanation: Structured check-ins give nurses a reliable voice to discuss operational roadblocks with directors. [learn more](GST321_U2_T5#GST321_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why is self-care considered a professional duty for nurses working in disaster zones?

options.A: It guarantees a higher salary during emergency deployments
options.B: It ensures the nurse remains healthy enough to provide safe patient care
options.C: It allows the nurse to avoid interacting with difficult patients
options.D: It proves to the hospital management that the nurse is working hard

explanation: A nurse who is completely burned out and emotionally depleted cannot effectively care for vulnerable patients. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h8)

question: Which of these is an example of biochemical data collected during a nutrition check?

options.A: Presence of muscle wasting
options.B: Body Mass Index score
options.C: Serum albumin levels
options.D: Daily water intake diary

explanation: You got it! Lab tests like serum albumin give us hard biochemical facts about protein levels inside the body.

question: Why is health education considered more effective than medical treatment alone in resource-limited settings?

options.A: It generates massive immediate revenue for local government councils
options.B: It stops illnesses from happening in the first place, saving scarce resources
options.C: It takes far less time and effort than prescribing drugs
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any medications in the village

explanation: Preventing a disease before it starts reduces the heavy financial and physical burden of treating advanced illnesses in areas with limited medical supplies. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T1#GNS214_U1_T1_h1)

question: During an IV insertion, what lets you know for sure that your needle has successfully entered the vein?

options.A: The infusion bag begins to drip rapidly without any pressure.
options.B: The surrounding skin turns pale and cool to the touch.
options.C: The patient reports a sudden cooling sensation in the arm.
options.D: A flash of blood appears inside the flashback chamber of the device.

explanation: That's right! Seeing that little 'flash' of dark red blood in the chamber is the classic sign that you're in the vein. Beautiful work!

question: Why should nurses look past a patient's physical impairment when providing total patient care?

options.A: To prevent the patient from asking too many questions
options.B: To address the social and emotional isolation that impairs recovery
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing mobility aids
options.D: To ensure the hospital bed is kept free for new admissions

explanation: Great thinking! Loneliness and unmet social needs can really slow down a patient's recovery. Holistic nursing means caring for the whole person.

question: Why do nurses constantly remind patients receiving radiation therapy not to wash off their skin treatment marks?

options.A: To prevent the patient from developing a severe skin allergy to the ink
options.B: To keep the hospital records accurate for billing and insurance purposes
options.C: To allow the radiation oncologists to track how fast the outer tumor is shrinking
options.D: To ensure precise daily alignment of the radiation beam to the exact tumor site

explanation: Spot on! Those little marks are like a bullseye. They make sure the radiation machine hits the exact tumor spot safely every single time.

question: What is a major cause of unsafe injection risks in informal healthcare settings?

options.A: Mandatory training for birth attendants
options.B: Too much government checking of pharmacies
options.C: An oversupply of safety boxes
options.D: Not enough clean, single-use equipment available

explanation: When places lack a steady supply of cheap, disposable syringes, dangerous reuse habits can creep in. Community health education helps fix this!

question: What style of training was mostly used in early Nigerian missionary hospitals?

options.A: Apprenticeship training
options.B: Military conscription
options.C: Online distance learning
options.D: University fellowship

explanation: You got it! Back then, nursing learners picked up practical skills through hands-on work right in the hospital wards, much like learning a trade.

question: Why do nurses train local leaders and teachers in mental health first aid?

options.A: To create a safety net that catches distress early before a full crisis occurs
options.B: To replace professional psychiatric nurses in community hospitals
options.C: To legally license everyday citizens to prescribe mental health drugs
options.D: To reduce the financial budget required for national health insurance

explanation: Training everyday leaders helps spot warning signs early, allowing for fast support before problems escalate. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h6)

question: How do fat-soluble (lipid-soluble) toxins act differently in the body compared to water-soluble ones?

options.A: They cross cell membranes easily and can build up in fatty tissues
options.B: They immediately break down into harmless gas inside the stomach
options.C: They cannot enter the bloodstream unless injected directly into a vein
options.D: They are filtered out by the kidneys almost immediately upon entry

explanation: Because they love fat, these toxins slip easily through cell barriers and can stay stored in fatty tissues for a long time, prolonging their effects.

question: In the quick AVPU neurological check scale, what does the letter 'V' stand for?

options.A: Venous pressure
options.B: Verbal response
options.C: Visual acuity
options.D: Ventilation rate

explanation: You got it! V stands for verbal—meaning the patient reacts or speaks when you talk to them.

question: Which inhalation device requires the patient to take a fast, forceful breath to activate medication delivery?

options.A: Dry Powder Inhaler
options.B: Metered-dose inhaler with spacer
options.C: Simple nasal cannula
options.D: Standard nebulizer machine

explanation: Dry Powder Inhalers rely entirely on the patient's own inhalation effort to pull the powder out of the device and into the lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h3)

question: What usually happens if food travels through the small intestine much faster than normal?

options.A: Increased vitamin storage in the liver
options.B: Reduced nutrient absorption and diarrhea
options.C: Higher than normal blood sugar spikes
options.D: Enhanced breakdown of complex proteins

explanation: When food rushes through too fast, digestive enzymes and cells don't get enough time to do their job, leaving unabsorbed nutrients to pull extra water into the stool.

question: What is the main job of a problem statement in your research proposal?

options.A: To provide a summary of the statistical results
options.B: To explain the background and why the issue needs attention
options.C: To offer final medical advice to patients
options.D: To list the personal biographies of the researchers

explanation: The problem statement tells your reader: 'Here is what is going wrong, here is why it matters, and here is why we need to fix it right now.'

question: How can public health nurses use incidence data to check if an immunization campaign worked?

options.A: By calculating the average age of patients in the ward
options.B: By measuring the total money spent on medical supplies
options.C: By checking if the number of new infections drops over time
options.D: By counting the total number of hospital beds available

explanation: If a vaccination drive is successful, you should see the number of new infections (incidence) go way down. Awesome nursing logic!

question: How does mindfulness meditation help people dealing with racing thoughts?

options.A: By teaching them to observe thoughts without judgment
options.B: By permanently erasing painful memories from the brain
options.C: By replacing emotional feelings with physical movement
options.D: By forcing the mind to stop thinking completely

explanation: Mindfulness isn't about clearing your head completely—it's about noticing your thoughts in the present moment without beating yourself up over them.

question: Why would a doctor prescribe the medication sucralfate for a duodenal ulcer?

options.A: It permanently neutralizes all digestive enzymes
options.B: It relaxes the pyloric sphincter to speed up digestion
options.C: It stimulates the pancreas to release more insulin
options.D: It forms a protective coating over the ulcer site

explanation: Great job! Sucralfate acts like a liquid bandage, sticking directly to the ulcer base to shield it from harsh stomach acids and pepsin.

question: Why is the retina at the back of the eye so important?

options.A: It produces the lubricating fluid inside the eyeball
options.B: It changes color to match the surrounding environment
options.C: It contains cells that turn light into nerve signals
options.D: It acts as a hard shield against physical injury

explanation: The retina holds special cells that catch light and change it into electrical signals for your brain to understand. Great job reviewing this!

question: What is the main safety perk of having a drug library built into a smart IV pump?

options.A: It alerts nurses when a dose falls outside safe clinical limits
options.B: It automatically orders new IV bags when fluid levels run low
options.C: It replaces the need to check patient IV insertion sites
options.D: It measures the exact urine output generated during the shift

explanation: You nailed it! The drug library acts like a safety checklist, warning you instantly if a programmed dose is too high or too low.

question: An order calls for 500 mg of Paracetamol. The available tablets are 250 mg each. How many tablets should the nurse give?

options.A: 2 tablets
options.B: 1 tablet
options.C: 0.5 tablet
options.D: 4 tablets

explanation: Using the formula: (500 mg / 250 mg) × 1 tablet = 2 tablets. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T6#GNS125_U2_T6_h4)

question: How do helminths (worms) generally differ from protozoa inside a human host?

options.A: Helminths are microscopic single cells that multiply rapidly in the blood
options.B: Helminths live exclusively on the outer surface of the skin
options.C: Helminths never produce eggs or larvae that leave the body
options.D: Helminths are multicellular worms that usually do not multiply inside the host

explanation: Spot on! Unlike tiny protozoa that keep multiplying inside your tissues, helminths are larger worms that lay eggs or larvae to spread instead.

question: What type of question is best for encouraging a patient to talk freely during a health counselling session?

options.A: Closed yes-or-no question
options.B: Leading accusation question
options.C: Strictly rhetorical question
options.D: Open-ended question

explanation: Open-ended questions (like "How do you feel about...?") give clients the floor to share their true thoughts instead of just nodding with a quick yes or no.

question: Which hormone keeps the uterus relaxed and quiet throughout most of pregnancy?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Estrogen
options.C: Prostaglandin
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Progesterone is like a chill pill for the uterus, keeping the muscles relaxed until it's time to meet the baby.

question: Which part of the Y-shaped antibody molecule binds directly to the antigen?

options.A: Complement tail
options.B: Fc region
options.C: Heavy chain stem
options.D: Fab region

explanation: Think of the Fab region as the hands of the antibody! The tips of the Y-shape have variable sequences that specifically match and grab onto antigens. You've got this!

question: What is the name of the primary federal legislation that guides quarantine enforcement in Nigeria?

options.A: The Quarantine Act
options.B: The Epidemic Control Code
options.C: The National Health Insurance Act
options.D: The Nursing and Midwifery Decree

explanation: The Quarantine Act is the established legal framework empowering Nigerian authorities to manage public health borders and restrictions. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the main job of a social worker on a community health team?

options.A: Reviewing lab results for abnormal electrolyte levels
options.B: Connecting families to housing and financial support
options.C: Performing surgical procedures in the clinic
options.D: Prescribing medications for high blood pressure

explanation: You got it! Social workers are pros at linking patients to resources outside the clinic that make daily life easier.

question: What is the normal baseline range for a healthy fetal heart rate?

options.A: 60 to 100 beats per minute
options.B: 110 to 160 beats per minute
options.C: 80 to 120 beats per minute
options.D: 140 to 200 beats per minute

explanation: Spot on! An unborn baby's heart beats much faster than an adult's, usually staying comfortably between 110 and 160 bpm.

question: Which of these is a great example of a non-drug (non-pharmacological) way to help a patient relax?

options.A: Providing a soothing back massage
options.B: Ordering a stronger dose of painkiller
options.C: Administering a standard dose of zolpidem
options.D: Increasing the intravenous fluid infusion rate

explanation: A gentle back rub helps relieve tension and promotes relaxation naturally, without any medication side effects.
